question: Which of the following shortcut keys can be used to quickly open a presentation in PowerPoint?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Ctrl + O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ctrl + O** is a universal shortcut used in several applications, including **Microsoft PowerPoint**, to **open an existing file or presentation.**
 
• This shortcut improves productivity by allowing users to access files quickly without navigating through menus manually.
 
• In the context of **Microsoft PowerPoint**, pressing **Ctrl + O** will directly open the "Open" dialog box, enabling users to browse and select a file to work on.
 
• It is part of the broader suite of **keyboard shortcuts** designed to enhance user efficiency within the **Microsoft Office** environment.
 
• The shortcut is widely recognized and standardized across various programs, making it a valuable tool for users familiar with **Windows-based applications.**
 
• Keyboard shortcuts like **Ctrl + O** reduce dependency on a mouse and are particularly beneficial for users aiming for **speed and accuracy.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Shift + O**__

 __
 
• This combination does not perform any specific function in **Microsoft PowerPoint**.
 
• In some software, **Shift** may modify other shortcut keys, but it is not associated with opening presentations.
 
 
 
• **Alt + O**__
 __
 
• **Alt + O** is not a default shortcut for opening files in **Microsoft PowerPoint**.
 
• In older versions of **Microsoft Word**, this combination was used to open the "Format" menu, but it has no relevance in PowerPoint.
 
 
 
• **Tab + O**__
 
 
• **Tab** is typically used for navigation purposes, such as moving between fields or options.
 
• It is not used in combination with **O** to open a file or presentation in PowerPoint.
